verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The display is one declaration, PhysicalResidualBridge.ScaledGraph.velocity, together with its evaluation map ScaledGraph.map — but matched in the chart variables, not the physical ones. In ScaledGraph.map (line 190) only the angular slot is physical (θ = p.2 1); for p = (t, (r, θ, z)) the other slots are chart-rescaled and the time slot is reversed: radius radialScale·r, axial radialScale·epsilon·z, time velocityScale·radialScale·epsilon·(1 − t), and last slot Y = (frequency·(radialScale·r)^exponent)•v_r + (velocityScale·radialScale·fastCoefficient·t)•v_t. For the instance the construction actually uses this is stated outright by commonGraph_map (PhysicalResidualBridge.lean:476): (commonGraph Q h i).map p = ((Q^(−1/2)·r, ((Q^(−D h)·z, (1 − t)/Q), cover^i (r^{d_r}•v_r + t•v_t))), θ). So the coordinate slots carry the (6.6) chart normalizations R = Q^(−1/2) r, Z = Q^(−D) z and T = (1 − t)/Q — the last being time-to-blowup, not t — and ScaledGraph.velocity a p = pack of velocityScale · a (G.map p) i (velocity_apply: G.velocity a p i = G.velocityScale * a (G.map p) i componentwise) adds the (6.1) velocity normalization in front of the value. Recovery: the Lean pair reads w(r,θ,z,t) = velocityScale · w̃(R, θ, Z, T, Y_i), which is the display composed with the (6.1)/(6.6) change of variables; the paper performs that change of variables separately, so the structural content of this display — the physical field is the chart field evaluated with its last argument slaved to the graph point Y — is exactly what ScaledGraph.map/velocity encode. This is the map the construction actually uses: PhysicalSignedWave.lean evaluates at `(commonGraph V.referenceScale V.exponent V.referenceCover).map z` in physicalPhase (:1029), physicalRaw (:1034) and physicalPressureCoefficient (:1252); the occurrences at :1223 and :1237 are hypotheses `… .map z ∈ B.strip.domain`, not evaluations. One further substantive encoding point: for commonGraph the Y slot is band-scaled, not absolute — commonGraph_radialScale gives frequency·(radialScale·r)^exponent = Λ_g^i·r^{d_r} and commonGraph_fastTimeScale gives velocityScale·radialScale·fastCoefficient = T_g^i, and since J_g v_r = Λ_g v_r, J_g v_t = T_g v_t (p. 63), the Y of G.map is J_g^i Y, the band representative Y_i of (6.5), not the absolute Y of (6.3). The two GraphCalculus declarations are the same formula in a reduced (r,t)-only, scalar-valued model: GraphCalculus.pullback F q = F (graph d vr vt q) with graph d vr vt q = (q, q.1^d • vr + q.2 • vt), matching (6.3) term for term but without θ, z and with F scalar. GraphRestriction.pullback F γ x = F x (γ x) is the display with the variable types left arbitrary, but I grepped NavierStokes/ for `GraphRestriction.pullback` and found no use at all outside its own file, so it is a generic definition the construction never instantiates. A second encoding point: neither `graph` nor `map` performs the paper's reduction (mod ℤ²) — the Y slot is a point of ℝ²; the reduction is carried separately by TorusAverages.quotientPoint and by the periodicity hypotheses used for the averages.
